correctness.rationale: Diagonalization on the exact normalized weighted Dirichlet monomial basis gives probability-barycenter numerical range. The downward support equals the maximum over eigenvalues and has a uniformly controlled Taylor expansion. A triangle from three genuine eigenvalues contains a centered disk whose radius lies between M/(1+a^k) and M, proving the optimal-radius asymptotic and full-dimensional interior. The three side-distance inequalities follow from fixed-angle separation and an a-dependent bound on the maximizing index. Explicit consecutive differences determine the leading maximum; endpoint continuity proves the phase law. Finite computations are corroborative only, not the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp centered inradius is an intrinsic quantitative invariant for a long-studied numerical-range family. The result determines the exponential collapse rate under vanishing argument and the nonconstant phase-dependent leading constant, a structural consequence invisible in qualitative zero-inclusion statements. It gives a natural complete small-angle asymptotic for all fixed moduli and for an entire family of weighted Dirichlet spaces without artificial parameter slicing.
